plan.title: Mouse liver HFD vs chow: DE genes and Hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: Raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 mice: 6 high-fat diet, 6 chow, liver, single batch, unpaired) are first checked for sample structure with a blind VST, PCA, and sample-distance heatmap, explicitly inspecting sample_01 whose library size is ~4x below the median rather than dropping it by default. DESeq2 then models raw counts with median-of-ratios normalization (never pre-scaled counts), a minimal count pre-filter, an explicit reference level (chow/control) and a named contrast (HFD vs chow), a Wald test, and apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold changes, selecting genes by BH-adjusted p-value (alpha 0.05) with independent filtering left on. The full ranked gene list (ranked by the Wald statistic) is then tested against the MSigDB mouse Hallmark collection with fgsea preranked GSEA, respecting the 15-500 gene set size window and collapsing redundant sets. A final report step assembles QC findings, DE results (with fit diagnostics and the low-depth sample's effect on the model explicitly discussed), and the Hallmark enrichment results with leading-edge genes and full reproducibility metadata.
